title: Latency-budgeted continuous allocator for asymmetric dialogues
creator: Asha Mohan
description: Background: In production traces we observe a high variance workload of asymmetric dialogues: short prompts followed by long responses and vice versa. Our current continuous allocator aggressively coalesces based on arrival time and slot availability which improves throughput but causes KV cache churn and tail latency spikes when long responses displace hot KV pages. Goal: implement a latency-budgeted allocator that makes per-request admission and residency decisions based on an explicit latency budget and predicted continuation length, reducing tail P99 latency by 20–40% for mixed-turn workloads while preserving >=90% of baseline throughput and limiting GPU memory variance to +/-10%.
acceptance_criteria: P99 latency for mixed-turn synthetic workload reduced by >=20% compared to mainline continuous allocator
Throughput (tokens/sec) remains within 90% of baseline for steady-state 2k concurrent connections
KV cache occupancy variance (across GPUs) reduced to +/-10% over a 30m window
No customer-facing errors introduced in canary (0.5% traffic) and automatic rollback triggers tested
Observability: per-request latency budget traces, KV residency logs, and GPU mem watermark metrics available in Console
design_decisions: Use a small per-request 'latency budget' metadata field computed at admission time from route SLO, current Q length, and historical token generation rate for the route

Partition allocator into fast-path (low-latency short answers) and slow-path (long-response optimistic coalescing). Fast-path favors immediate slot assignment with reserved KV window; slow-path batches more aggressively but pre-reserves KV pages and marks requests as 'warmable' for prefix caching

Introduce KV residency tiers: pinned (high probability hot prefixes), reserved (soft reservation for ongoing long responses), and ephemeral (evictable). Admission decides tier based on predicted continuation length and latency budget
Throttle continuous coalescing by injecting a time-decay admission penalty when a GPU's KV eviction rate exceeds a dynamic threshold to avoid oscillatory evictions

Estimator model: light-weight heuristic combining route-level percentiles and recently observed generation throughput; keep model deterministic and cheap to compute in the allocator loop (no RPCs to ML components)

Fallback policy: if predicted long-response path cannot satisfy latency budget, immediately route to compatible lower-latency model variant (e.g., quantized or smaller context) via smart routing layer
implementation_notes: Allocator changes live in runtime/slot_allocator: add LatencyBudget struct and admission flow modifications
KV controller: add soft_reserve(kbytes) API to runtime/kv_manager so allocator can mark pages reserved for a slot without immediate pinning
GPU memory accounting: expose per-GPU eviction_rate, pinned_bytes, reserved_bytes metrics to scheduler via exporter interface
Telemetry: emit event for each admission decision with fields [route, pred_cont_len, latency_budget_ms, chosen_tier, reserved_bytes, timestamp]
Simulation harness: extend perf-sim to generate asymmetric dialogues with tunable short/long-turn ratios and validate eviction dynamics before canary

Config: add runtime flags for default_latency_budget_ms (per-tier), eviction_threshold_bytes, and coalescing_penalty_factor; make defaults conservative behind feature flag 'latency_budgeted_allocator'
testing_plan: Unit tests for admission heuristics and tier selection with synthetic distributions
Integration tests in k8s dev cluster with 4-GPU node shapes reproducing mixed-turn traffic profile
Perf-sim runs comparing mainline and new allocator across 1000 simulated clients for 1 hour; capture P50/P95/P99 token latency, KV evictions, and GPU memory variance
Canary: deploy to hostpool-canary with 0.5% traffic for 24 hours with auto-rollback on P99 regression >10%
Chaos test: introduce deliberate KV eviction storm (simulate sudden burst of long responses) and verify coalescing_penalty prevents tail amplification
rollout_plan: Stage 1: feature flag enabled in internal staging, run perf-sim and manual validation (1 week)
Stage 2: Canary 0.5% production traffic, monitor for 24–48 hours; keep automatic rollback thresholds configured
Stage 3: Gradual ramp to 10% over 3 days if metrics stable; collect route-level regressions and customer-impact signals
Stage 4: Full migration for routes marked as mixed-turn heavy; for other routes keep default allocator unless route config explicitly opts in
Stage 5: Post-rollout tuning sweep (2 weeks) to adjust penalty factors and reserved sizing based on observed real traffic
